title: Check yourself: Least privilege for Bedrock and Vertex

questions.stem: A policy allows bedrock:* on * for an application's role. A reviewer asks for least privilege. Which rewrite fits?

options.text: Keep the policy as written and add a condition that requires SSL
options.says: Ruled out because conditions come after the basics: "defining the actions that can be taken on specific resources under specific conditions".

options.text: Keep the wildcard action but name the single model's ARN in the resource
options.says: Ruled out because a wildcard action still grants more than "the permissions required to perform a task".

options.text: Replace the wildcard with a deny statement for every other model
options.says: Ruled out because "By default, users and roles don't have permission to create or modify Amazon Bedrock resources", so a policy should add what is needed and not rely on denies.

options.text: List the one invoke action and name the single model's ARN
options.says: The page says to "grant only the permissions required to perform a task", by "defining the actions that can be taken on specific resources".

questions.stem: A service account must only call a Claude endpoint on Google Cloud. The team compares a ready-made grant bundle with one it authors. What does the page favour?

options.text: The tailored role with just the predict permission
options.says: The page says "custom roles are recommended because you create them, so you can limit their access to only the permissions that are required".

options.text: A predefined role, since the platform maintains it for the team
options.says: Ruled out because "Predefined roles often contain more permissions than you need."

options.text: A basic role such as Editor, since it covers every service at once
options.says: Ruled out because basic roles "provide access control to your Agent Platform resources at the project level, and are common to all Google Cloud services", which is broad.

options.text: No role at all, since a service account works without any grant
options.says: Ruled out because "You grant access by assigning IAM roles to principals."

questions.stem: A team adds the deploy permission to its invoker role just in case. What does the Google page warn?

options.text: It blocks the predict permission until the deploy one is removed
options.says: Ruled out because the same sentence shows the predict permission grants "the ability to call the endpoint for predictions" on its own.

options.text: It makes every prediction slower on the endpoint that holds it
options.says: Ruled out because the predict permission "grants the service account the ability to call the endpoint for predictions", and the page says nothing of speed.

options.text: It opens a route to exporting other models held in the project
options.says: The page warns that the deploy permission "might allow a user to export other deployed or deployable models from the project".

options.text: It has no effect at all, because deploy only adds serving capacity
options.says: Ruled out because the warning is that it "might allow a user to export other deployed or deployable models from the project".
